title: Compact [C II] emitters around a C IV absorption complex at redshift 5.7
question: What are the properties and environment of galaxies associated with a complex high-ionization C IV absorption system at redshift z ≈ 5.7 toward QSO J1030+0524?

data.sensitivity: 31 μJy per beam (1σ continuum); 4.1 and 4.2 mJy km s^-1 per beam (1σ in 4-channel / 66 km s^-1 moment-0 maps at [C II]1030A and B)

what.value: Four Lyα emitters (LAEs) discovered with VLT/MUSE within ±1500 km s^-1 of the C IV absorbers

evidence.quote: Figures 1a and 2d mark these LAEs (purple circles) detected within ± 1500 km s − 1 of the C iv absorbers with the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explore (MUSE) on the Very Large Telescope (VLT) [5].

what.value: Published CO Schechter luminosity functions for z = 0 to 6 used to estimate expected foreground CO interloper counts

evidence.quote: Using published CO luminosity functions for the redshift range between 0 and 6 [37], we estimated that the expected number of CO sources within the whole datacube should be approximately 0.4 sources.

what.value: Optical coordinates of background QSO J1030+0524

evidence.quote: centered on the optical coordinate of the background QSO J1030+0524 (10 h 30 m 27 s . 092, +05 ◦ 24 ′ 55 . 02 '' ; [33])

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA mosaic datacubes and continuum
recipe.method: Standard CASA pipeline calibration followed by CASA tclean imaging of the 7-pointing mosaic with natural weighting and a Gaussian uv-taper to circularize the beam; collapse 4 channels over 66 km s^-1 for moment-0 maps.
key_parameters: moment-0 collapsed over 4 channels (62.5 MHz; ≈ 66 km s^-1)
survey radius ≈ 23" where primary beam response > 20%

recipe.goal: Blind search for emission lines and fidelity assessment
recipe.method: Run findclumps top-hat convolution over 4 to 17 channels on the datacubes for positive and negative peaks, crop duplicates within 1" and 280 MHz, fit an error function to positive/negative peak counts to compute detection fidelity, and verify detections by splitting data by polarization (XX vs YY), mosaic pointings, and exposure time halves.
key_parameters: frequency window sizes = 4 to 17 channels (≈ 66–282 km s^-1)
duplicate cropping offsets = 1" and 280 MHz (300 km s^-1)
assumptions: Relevant velocity interval for absorber association is ±700 km s^-1 around each absorber (contiguous 2280 km s^-1 interval)

recipe.goal: Identify line transition and estimate low-z CO interloper probability
recipe.method: Calculate expected number counts of foreground CO(3-2) to CO(8-7) interlopers brighter than [C II]1030A in the survey volume using published Schechter luminosity functions, and compute probability of two interlopers falling within the 2280 km s^-1 velocity window.
key_parameters: Survey volume: circular radius 23" across 4 SPWs (7380 km s^-1 total velocity interval)
assumptions: CO(6-5) luminosity function at z = 2 also applies to CO(7-6) and CO(8-7)

recipe.goal: Measure [C II] line properties, FIR continuum upper limits, and derive SFRs
recipe.method: Extract 1D spectra within 0.24" radius of peak position, fit a single Gaussian profile, correct for primary beam response and 20% aperture loss, and convert [C II] luminosities and 2σ continuum upper limits to SFRs.
assumptions: Flat ΛCDM cosmology with Ω_Λ = 0.69, Ω_M = 0.31, H_0 = 67.7 km s^-1 Mpc^-1
νL_ν / L_IR = 0.13 at ν = 1900 GHz (modified blackbody with β = 1.8, T_dust = 41 K)
SFR_IR (M_sun yr^-1) = 1.01 x 10^-10 L_IR (L_sun) for Chabrier IMF

recipe.goal: Fit C IV and Si IV Voigt profiles in QSO J1030+0524 spectra
recipe.method: Reduce VLT/X-Shooter and Magellan/FIRE spectra, normalize continuum via iterative cubic spline fits, and simultaneously fit a hierarchical Voigt profile model of 3 absorption components convolved to instrument resolutions using MCMC.
key_parameters: X-Shooter spectral resolution λ/Δλ = 5300 (0.9" slit); FIRE spectral resolution λ/Δλ = 6000 (0.6" slit)
assumptions: Redshifts of C IV and Si IV components are constrained to align in velocity space

recipe.goal: Search for rest-frame UV and Lyα counterparts in HST and VLT/MUSE data
recipe.method: Co-add HST images with DrizzlePac and perform 0.7"-diameter aperture photometry at [C II] positions and random sky positions; reduce MUSE cube with MUSE pipeline and CubEx, calibrate astrometry via HST F775W and Gaia, and search for Lyα within 3" and ±500 km s^-1.
key_parameters: MUSE search radius ≈ 3" (20 pkpc) and ±500 km s^-1
assumptions: SFR_FUV (M_sun yr^-1) = 0.72 x 10^-28 L_ν (erg s^-1 Hz^-1)
